name: FlureeDB
tagline: Immutable RDF graph database with time travel, git-style branching, SPARQL, JSON-LD and Cypher.
description: Fluree DB is a ledger-style graph database: every transaction becomes an immutable, content-addressed commit, so any query can run against any past state, and a dataset can be branched, rebased and merged much like a Git repository. Data is RDF and can be queried with SPARQL, Fluree's JSON-LD query syntax or openCypher, with BM25 full-text, HNSW vector and geo search plus triple-level access policies built into the engine. Version 4.0 (April 2026) is a Rust rewrite of the original Clojure system and ships under BSL 1.1, with each release converting to Apache 2.0 four years after it ships; v5 is in alpha. Reach for it when provenance and history matter: auditable knowledge graphs, regulated data sharing, and persistent memory for AI agents.

license.name: Business Source License 1.1 (converts to Apache 2.0 after 4 years)

pricing.notes: Self-hosting is free except for offering it as a competing hosted database service; Fluree's cloud has a usage-limited free tier.

scale.notes: Vendor benchmarks load the full 21.5-billion-triple Wikidata dump on a single commodity server; no built-in sharding.

strengths: Every commit is immutable and queryable by transaction number, timestamp or commit ID
Git-style branch, rebase and merge workflows for datasets
One engine answers SPARQL, JSON-LD and openCypher with the same features
BM25, HNSW vector and geo search participate in joins and filters like any graph pattern
Triple-level access policies enforced inside the query engine
Reproducible vendor benchmarks against QLever, Virtuoso, Neo4j and others are published
weaknesses: BSL license forbids offering it as a hosted database service to third parties
v4 is a 2026 rewrite, so client libraries, tooling and community answers are still thin
No horizontal sharding; scale-out means running separate ledgers
RDF modelling has a learning curve for teams used to property graphs or SQL
useCases: Auditable knowledge graphs with full history
Long-term memory for AI coding agents and assistants
Semantic data integration with RDF and JSON-LD
Shared datasets that need branching and review before merge
notIdealFor: Teams that require an OSI-approved license today
